newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Commission meets on expansion to the east.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission meets on expansion to the east.

text.p: The European Commission met on Tuesday to formalise the list of countries it thinks should be asked to take part in the European Union's first enlargement behind the former Iron Curtain.
No surprises were expected with Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia and Estonia to be asked to join Cyprus in the EU's most ambitious expansion since its foundation.

A document setting out the expansion plan and the policy changes the EU will have to make to accommodate radically different countries says that five other applicants -- Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, Bulgaria and Romania -- should be left to prepare for membership at their own pace.
Cyprus had already been promised membership talks this year.
The document, to be presented formally to the European Parliament on Wednesday, will tell the East European applicants they have to make more economic efforts before they cross the threshold.

The changes precribed in the paper for the existing 15-nation EU involve a new inter-governmental conference soon after 2000 to overhaul the EU's decision-making procedures to prevent paralysis in a bloc with 21 members.

The EU's June 16-17 Amsterdam summit failed to agree on how to revise the way decisions are taken ahead of enlargement, but said a new overhaul would be necessary if the bloc extended to more than 20 members.
A radical reform of the EU's Common Agriculture Policy is also prescribed in the document, with drastic cuts of 10 percent in EU guaranteed prices for milk and 20 percent for cereals.
The EU executive says the EU should live under the current ceiling of the member states' financing until 2006.
The Commission's proposal will not be the last word on who will negotiate EU entry as it could be overturned by EU governments, who have different national interests at stake.
A final decision will be taken by EU leaders at their Luxembourg summit in December.
